questions.q: What two inputs does the External Services setup wizard need to register a third-party API?
options: A WSDL document and a Connected App
A Workflow Rule and an Outbound Message
A Named Credential and the API's OpenAPI (OAS) specification
A Platform Event definition and a Permission Set
questions.explain: The wizard uses a Named Credential for the endpoint and authentication, plus the third-party API's OpenAPI specification, to generate the service.

questions.q: What does External Services generate for each operation defined in the imported OpenAPI spec?
options: A custom platform event and a subscriber trigger
A WSDL file only
A Workflow Rule and an Outbound Message
An invocable Flow action and Apex stub classes grouped under "dynamic classes"
questions.explain: Each operation in the spec produces both a no-code invocable Flow action and Apex stub classes usable directly in code.

questions.q: According to Salesforce's own guidance referenced in this lesson, what do you NOT need to write for the generated External Service code?
options: Unit tests for the generated code itself, since it was produced by the platform from the spec
A Named Credential
Any business logic calling the generated action
Integration tests against the real third-party service
questions.explain: Because the code is generated directly from the spec, Salesforce's guidance says you don't need to unit test the generated code — you still need integration tests and the business logic that uses it.

questions.q: Where do External Services' auto-generated Apex classes appear in Setup?
options: Under Remote Site Settings
Under the Apex Classes list, grouped as "dynamic classes"
Under Workflow Rules
They are not visible anywhere in Setup
questions.explain: The generated stub classes show up under a "dynamic classes" grouping within the Apex Classes list.

questions.q: When might a hand-written Apex callout (Chapter 1) still be preferred over External Services?
options: Only when the API uses SOAP instead of REST
Whenever the third-party API happens to use JSON
When no usable OpenAPI spec exists, the behavior needs custom logic the generated stubs can't express cleanly, or fine-grained control matters more than generation speed
External Services should always be preferred, with no exceptions
questions.explain: External Services is ideal when a usable spec exists and generated code suffices; hand-written callouts still earn their place for custom logic, missing specs, or fine-grained control.
